description: The WHEN OTHER default arm of the top-level dispatcher at app/cbl/COCRDSLC.cbl:373-380 - the fifth and last arm of the ordered EVALUATE TRUE at :304, the program's only abend-shaped path, and the ONLY ONE OF THE TWENTY CASES IN THIS FOLDER IN WHICH NO MAP IS SENT. REACHABILITY IS THE SUBJECT OF THIS CASE AND IT IS PROVED RATHER THAN ASSERTED. CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT is PIC 9(01) at app/cpy/COCOM01Y.cpy:29 carrying exactly two condition names - 88 CDEMO-PGM-ENTER VALUE 0 at :30 and 88 CDEMO-PGM-REENTER VALUE 1 at :31 - so the digits 2 through 9 are every one of them representable and match NEITHER. That single fact is the whole key to this arm, and the inbound state declared below is chosen to clear three separate obstacles standing between it and the arm. (1) THE AID COERCION AT :291-299. SET PFK-INVALID TO TRUE; IF CCARD-AID-ENTER OR CCARD-AID-PFK03 SET PFK-VALID TO TRUE; IF PFK-INVALID SET CCARD-AID-ENTER TO TRUE. After that block the AID is NECESSARILY either ENTER or PFK03, because every one of the other fourteen CCARD-AID conditions app/cpy/CVCRD01Y.cpy declares on the PIC X(5) item is folded onto ENTER. So this arm cannot be reached by pressing an unusual key - sibling case17 pins that fold with DFHCLEAR and case18 with DFHPF15 - and the AID declared here is DFHENTER, which survives the block untouched; a PF3 press would have matched arm A1 instead. (2) THE RE-INITIALISATION AT :268-272. IF EIBCALEN IS EQUAL TO 0 OR (CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM = LIT-MENUPGM AND NOT CDEMO-PGM-REENTER) INITIALIZE CARDDEMO-COMMAREA, WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA. INITIALIZE sets a PIC 9 item to ZERO, which would make CDEMO-PGM-ENTER true and route the run to arm A3 instead. The trap is the second disjunct: at context 2 the term NOT CDEMO-PGM-REENTER is TRUE, so an origin of COMEN01C - LIT-MENUPGM at :179-180 - would satisfy that disjunct on its own and destroy the very state this case exists to reach. EIBCALEN is therefore 172, which is the 160-byte CARDDEMO-COMMAREA (4+8+4+8+8+1+1+9+25+25+25+11+1+16+7+7) plus the 12-byte WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA trailer at :200-203, CA-FROM-PROGRAM X(8) and CA-FROM-TRANID X(4); and the origin is not COMEN01C, so the ELSE at :273-278 runs and splits bytes 1-160 into the commarea and bytes 161-172 into the trailer by reference modification. (3) THE FOUR PRECEDING ARMS. The origin is deliberately CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM 'COCRDLIC' with CDEMO-FROM-TRANID 'CCLI' - LIT-CCLISTPGM at :171-172 and LIT-CCLISTTRANID at :173-174, the card-list origin - and it carries a fully validated selection: account 00000000050 and card 0500024453765740, which are the CARD-ACCT-ID and CARD-NUM of fixture row 0. That is a STRONGER assertion than a neutral origin would be, because arm A2 at :339-340 is WHEN CDEMO-PGM-ENTER AND CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM EQUAL LIT-CCLISTPGM, so a matching origin ALONE MUST NOT FIRE IT: the AND CDEMO-PGM-ENTER conjunct is false at context 2 and the arm has to be passed over. This case therefore proves the conjunction is genuinely evaluated rather than short-circuited on the origin, which is exactly what gate G30 asks of an ordered EVALUATE - and it is what makes the not-invoked read below mean something, since the record the program would have fetched is sitting in the inbound commarea and is still never fetched. WALKING :304 IN SOURCE ORDER (gate G30, rule R7): A1 WHEN CCARD-AID-PFK03 at :305 - no, the AID is ENTER; A2 at :339-340 - no, the origin matches but the conjunct does not; A3 WHEN CDEMO-PGM-ENTER at :349 - no; A4 WHEN CDEMO-PGM-REENTER at :357 - no; therefore WHEN OTHER at :373. The arm is reachable ONLY through a corrupt or out-of-band context digit, which is to say it is a genuine defensive branch the author wrote against a state this program's own callers cannot produce. It is preserved exactly as found rather than optimised away (practice B5, requirement I5). THE ARM, STATEMENT BY STATEMENT. :374 MOVE LIT-THISPGM TO ABEND-CULPRIT - X(8) 'COCRDSLC' into X(8), exact, with neither padding nor truncation. :375 MOVE '0001' TO ABEND-CODE - X(4), and note that this is the four-CHARACTER STRING 0001 rather than a number, so it is never rendered as 1. :376 MOVE SPACES TO ABEND-REASON - X(50), fifty spaces. :377-378 MOVE 'UNEXPECTED DATA SCENARIO' TO WS-RETURN-MSG - a 24-character literal into the PIC X(75) item declared at :134, so it is RIGHT-PADDED WITH 51 SPACES, and 24 + 51 = 75 sums mechanically (rule R5: a PIC X receiver pads and truncates on the right; practice B11). :379-380 PERFORM SEND-PLAIN-TEXT THRU SEND-PLAIN-TEXT-EXIT. ABEND-DATA IS MUTATED AND THEN NEVER TRANSMITTED. app/cpy/CSMSG02Y.cpy:21-29 declares it as ABEND-CODE X(4) plus ABEND-CULPRIT X(8) plus ABEND-REASON X(50) plus ABEND-MSG X(72), and 4 + 8 + 50 + 72 = 134 (practice B11). The only statement in the program that sends it is in ABEND-ROUTINE - EXEC CICS SEND FROM(ABEND-DATA) LENGTH(LENGTH OF ABEND-DATA) NOHANDLE at :865-869 - and ABEND-ROUTINE is a SEPARATE, CICS-NATIVE path reached only when CICS drives the HANDLE ABEND LABEL armed at :250-252, a path that ends in EXEC CICS HANDLE ABEND CANCEL at :871-873 and EXEC CICS ABEND ABCODE('9999') at :875-877. It is NOT reached from here. So the visible output of this arm is the 75-byte plain text ALONE: the culprit, the code 0001 and the fifty blank reason bytes are internal state that no channel in this model carries, and they are deliberately NOT declared as a 134-byte record in expectedMessages. Two consequences are pinned in their place - expectedReturnCode is 0, and no common.AbendException is raised. READ THE RETURN CODE CAREFULLY: DESPITE THE ABEND-* FIELD NAMES, THIS PATH DOES NOT ABEND. COCRDSLC contains ZERO occurrences of CALL 'CEE3ABD', verified by exhaustive search of the source, so gate G35 has no call site anywhere in this program; the task ends normally through the EXEC CICS RETURN inside SEND-PLAIN-TEXT. One further oddity is recorded for accuracy and marked clearly as NOT EXERCISED HERE (practice B5): CSMSG02Y declares all four of its items VALUE SPACES, and the INITIALIZE at :254-256 names CC-WORK-AREA, WS-MISC-STORAGE and WS-COMMAREA but NOT ABEND-DATA, so ABEND-MSG holds spaces and never LOW-VALUES - which means ABEND-ROUTINE's IF ABEND-MSG EQUAL LOW-VALUES guard at :859-861 can never pass and the default text it would have moved is unreachable dead text. SEND-PLAIN-TEXT AT :838-851, AND WHY NO MAP APPEARS. EXEC CICS SEND TEXT FROM(WS-RETURN-MSG) LENGTH(LENGTH OF WS-RETURN-MSG) ERASE FREEKB at :839-844 transmits exactly 75 bytes, and :846-847 is then a BARE EXEC CICS RETURN with no TRANSID and no COMMAREA. Four consequences follow and each is a distinguishing assertion of this case. FIRST, 1000-SEND-MAP at :412-421 never runs, so the CCRDSLA map is never built: not one of the fifteen xxxO items of app/cpy-bms/COCRDSL.CPY - the two title lines, the date and the time, the transaction and program names, the two search criteria, the four card-detail fields, the information line, the error line and the function-key line - is painted, and this case therefore declares an EMPTY sends list where the other nineteen declare one send. If a title literal or a date-and-time header appears here, the case is wrong. The transmitted text is reported instead on the variable-width DISPLAY_LINE channel, which is the honest channel for a SEND TEXT: it is a line the program emitted rather than a screen field it painted, and DISPLAY_LINE is the only one of the three channels whose width is not fixed at 78 or 80. SECOND, 1400-SEND-SCREEN at :563-567 never runs, so CCARD-NEXT-MAPSET and CCARD-NEXT-MAP are never written at :565-566 and SET CDEMO-PGM-REENTER TO TRUE at :567 NEVER EXECUTES - CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT is pinned below UNCHANGED AT 2, still holding the out-of-band digit it arrived with, which is also why no next mapset and no next map appear on the response. THIRD, COMMON-RETURN at :394-406 never runs, so MOVE WS-RETURN-MSG TO CCARD-ERROR-MSG at :395 does not happen, WS-COMMAREA is never laid out at :397-400, and the EXEC CICS RETURN TRANSID(LIT-THISTRANID) COMMAREA(WS-COMMAREA) LENGTH(LENGTH OF WS-COMMAREA), which is 2000 bytes at :402-406, does not happen either. The termination pinned below is therefore RETURN_NO_TRANSID and emphatically not RETURN_TRANSID: the response names no next program, no next mapset and no next map, and there is no transaction for a commarea to be carried back to, so the pseudo-conversation ENDS. For gate G37 and rule R6 the point is sharper than usual - the commarea as it stood IS carried on the payload, which is the only reason the out-of-band digit is assertable at all, but there is no continuation, and here as everywhere in this migration no server-side session either way. FOURTH, SEND-LONG-TEXT at :820-833 is NOT used: it is unreachable dead code whose only operand, WS-LONG-MSG PIC X(500) at :125, is referenced nowhere else in the program, and it must never be confused with SEND-PLAIN-TEXT (practice B5). THE DEAD POST-EVALUATE BLOCK AT :386-391, WITH BOTH READINGS STATED HONESTLY (practice B12). This arm is the only one of the five that does not end in GO TO COMMON-RETURN, which is structurally why the IF INPUT-ERROR / MOVE WS-RETURN-MSG TO CCARD-ERROR-MSG / PERFORM 1000-SEND-MAP / GO TO COMMON-RETURN block after END-EVALUATE exists at all. It is nevertheless not reached, for two INDEPENDENT reasons, and both are given rather than one. The first is that the EXEC CICS RETURN inside SEND-PLAIN-TEXT TERMINATES THE CICS TASK, so control never comes back from the PERFORM and the statements after END-EVALUATE at :381 are never executed; in the translation that is a return from the handler at exactly that point. The second is that even if control did come back the guard would be false: INITIALIZE WS-MISC-STORAGE at :254-256 sets WS-INPUT-FLAG PIC X(1) at :51 to SPACES while 88 INPUT-ERROR is VALUE '1' at :53, so INPUT-ERROR does not hold. Nor does 88 INPUT-PENDING VALUE LOW-VALUES at :54 - after INITIALIZE the flag is spaces and matches NONE of its three condition names, another preserved quirk (practice B5). No edit paragraph runs on this path at all: 2000-PROCESS-INPUTS, 2210-EDIT-ACCOUNT and 2220-EDIT-CARD are all skipped, so no filter flag is set and neither CC-WORK-AREA REDEFINES accessor is exercised - gate G34 has no site in this case. NO DATASET ACCESS. 9000-READ-DATA is never performed, so card.CardRepository.readByCardNumber IS NOT INVOKED - the only case in this folder in which even the live keyed read is absent, and the reason the coherent card-list selection in the inbound commarea matters. readByAccountIdViaAltIndex is not invoked either: 9150-GETCARD-BYACCT at :779-812 is unreachable dead code, the only occurrences of 9150 in the whole program being its own two labels, so the CARDAIX alternate-index path is never executed by this program on ANY path. CARDAIX is a second finder over the one CARDDAT base cluster and never a second table, so no CARDAIX input is declared (gate G45, practice B5). Gate G47 has no site here either, because no RESP is produced. The three CARDDAT rows are seeded from the DERIVED TEST COPY under fixtures/ for uniformity with the other nineteen cases and never from app/data/ASCII/carddata.txt, which is read-only parity oracle (practice B3), and they are pinned unchanged on the final-state channel because this program issues no WRITE, no REWRITE and no DELETE. The clock is pinned to 2022-07-19T23:16:00 and carried for uniformity (practice B7) even though this path paints no date-and-time header at all, and the code page is named US-ASCII explicitly rather than inherited from the platform (practice B8); IBM037 belongs to app/data/EBCDIC and is out of scope. THE NAME SAYS SELECT; THE PROGRAM IS A DETAIL VIEW. Rule R1 keeps the mandated class name and takes behaviour from the source, so the divergence is DOCUMENTED AND NOT CORRECTED (practice B4, register 0.8.4), and three independent artefacts corroborate it: the source's own :4 header reads 'Function: Accept and process credit card detail request'; README.md:213-231 lists transaction CCDL against COCRDSLC as a card view rather than a selector; and app/csd/CARDDEMO.CSD:219-220 defines PROGRAM(COCRDSLC) with DESCRIPTION(VIEW CARD DETAIL). PROVENANCE (practice B12): every expected value here was derived by structured reading of app/cbl/COCRDSLC.cbl:248-300, :304-392, :838-851 and :857-880, of app/cpy/COCOM01Y.cpy:19-44, of app/cpy/CSMSG02Y.cpy:21-29 and of app/cpy/CVCRD01Y.cpy, cross-checked against the app/cpy-bms/COCRDSL.CPY xxxI widths, app/bms/COCRDSL.bms and the real ASCII fixture - NEVER captured from a live COBOL execution, which plan 0.7.6 proves impossible in this environment with eight verified blockers (risk R-A). GATES. This is the twentieth and last file of gate G15 for this program, and it completes gate G18, whose module verdict is the conjunction of zero diffs across all twenty. It contributes to G30 (the WHEN OTHER default, and the proof that A2's AND conjunct is genuinely evaluated), to G37 (statelessness under a terminating, commarea-less return), to G45 secondarily (no alternate-index access) and to G51 (the controller is reached as a plain Java object, with no MockMvc, no servlet container and no JobLauncher in the path). Gates G32, G35 and G39 do not apply: all nine GO TOs in this program are forward early-exit or shared-terminal jumps and CBSTM03A alone forms backward loops; there is no CALL 'CEE3ABD' here; and the map declares no PAGENO item. G19 and G21 have no site because no record is written, G34 none because no REDEFINES accessor runs, G38 none because no map is built and no attribute byte is set, G40 none because no XCTL is taken, and G47 none because no RESP is produced. Rule R4 has no site either - COCRDSLC holds no PIC 9(n)V(n) monetary field - so gates G22 through G28 are not exercised by this case.
